question_text: 3. The ELITE-SYMPHONY trial, published in 2007, evaluated the efficacy of four different immunosuppressive regimens: low-dose cyclosporine, versus standard dose cyclosporine, versus low-dose tacrolimus, versus low-dose sirolimus. All patients also received induction therapy with daclizumab, as well as mycophenolate mofetil and corticosteroids. Allograft survival was significantly higher in the low-dose tacrolimus group compared to both the standard-dose cyclosporine and low-dose sirolimus groups. Since its publication, this trial has played a pivotal role in shaping current standards for routine maintenance immunosuppression. Regarding immunosuppressive therapy for kidney transplant, which of the following statements is correct?

options.A: Currently, the more commonly used induction therapy agents include anti-thymocyte globulin (ATG) and basiliximab. Basiliximab exerts its effect by inhibiting the interleukin-3 (IL-3) receptor, which is also known as signal 3.
options.B: Tacrolimus affect the synthesis of purine thus cause the arrest of cell cycle. It had been the backbone of immunosuppressive therapy for kidney transplant.
options.C: The calcium dependent signaling induced by TCR stimulation is known as signal 1. ATG exerts its immunosuppressive effects in part by interfering signal 1.
options.D: Sirolimus may cause adverse effect such as neurotoxicity and increased the risk of malignancy.

A 58-year-old woman was sent to emergent department due to cough, fever and loss of smell since 3 days ago. She is well except with medical history of hypertension under regular angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitor treatment for 5 years. At ER, her vital signs as body temperature 38.1°C, heart rate was 102 beats/min, respiratory rate 18/min, and blood pressure 152/94 mm Hg. The diagnosis of SARS-CoV-2 infection was confirmed by PCR. Laboratory data was collected as follows:
Plasma: Na+ 135, K+ 2.9, Cl- 111, BUN 32, Cr 1.9, CRP 6.3, Albumin 3.2
Urine: Glucose Negative, Protein 2+, RBC 10-20 /HPF, Osmolality 288, Cr 70, Na+ 77, K+ 18, Cl- 96

1. Which one of the following statements concerning the SARS-CoV-2 induced AKI is NOT CORRECT?

options.A: The incidence of AKI in COVID-19 infected patients according to KDIGO criteria is relative high and more severe compared to the previous SARS and MERS-CoV infections.
options.B: High CRP levels indicated SARS-CoV-2 induced systemic inflammation which can contribute to the development of acute kidney injury (AKI)
options.C: The direct cytopathic effect of SARS-CoV-2 on kidney is one of the pathogenesis of AKI in COVID-19 patients.
options.D: According to postmortem autopsies that the main kidney damage is at the tubulointerstitium with vary degrees of acute tubular necrosis and varying degrees of lymphocyte infiltration.

question_text:
A 35 year-old female with end-stage renal disease secondary to herb nephropathy who has been on continuous ambulatory peritoneal dialysis for 3 years is brought to the emergency room because of increasing shortness of breath over the past 3 weeks. Her dialysis prescription is four exchanges per day using 2 L of dialysate per exchange. Physical examination shows an anxious female with pulse rate of 110 per minute, respiration rate of 18 per minute, and blood pressure of 142/92 mmHg. Her neck veins are slightly distended. Chest examination shows dullness over the entire right chest posteriorly to percussion. She has no edema. Chest roentgenogram reveals a large amount of right pleural effusion. A thoracocentesis is done; the fluid is found to have a protein content of 3.6 g/dL, LDH 250 IU/L, glucose 180 mg/dL, WBC 500/μL, Neutrophil 40%, lymphocyte 55% and RBC 100/μL.
Which one is the best management for the patient?

options.A: Discontinuation of peritoneal dialysis and initiation of hemodialysis
options.B: Surgical exploration to locate and repair the diaphragmatic leak
options.C: Insertion of a tube for drainage and arrange thoracoscopy
options.D: Pleurodesis and instillation of minocycline into the pleural cavity

question_text: A 65-year-old patient presented to ER with severe abdominal pain. He received radical cystectomy, urethrectomy, and ileum conduit urinary diversion for urothelial cancer 3 years ago. He took metformin 500mg 1# TID for diabetes mellitus, irbesartan 150mg 1# QD for hypertension, and benzbromarone 50mg 1# QD for hyperuricemia. Urine analysis revealed: WBC >100/HPF, RBC 50-100/HPF, protein 3+, and bacteria 4+. CT imaging of the abdomen and KUB are shown as follows. Which one of the followings is the MOST LIKELY major composition of the stone in ileum conduit in the imaging?

options.A: Calcium oxalate
options.B: Uric acid
options.C: Magnesium ammonium phosphate
options.D: Cysteine

question_text:
A 67-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease on automated peritoneal dialysis (APD) for 9 years presented to the emergency department with generalized weakness, vomiting, and poor appetite for one week. The vomiting was non-bilious and not related to food intake. She also reported atypical abdominal pain, anorexia, and constipation. Physical examination and imaging revealed ascites, and peritoneal fluid analysis demonstrated bloody dialysate with a white blood cell count of 200/μL and 83% lymphocytes. Dialysate culture was negative. A computed tomography (CT) scan of the abdomen revealed a calcified fibrous cocoon encasing the bowel, extensive peritoneal thickening, and intra-abdominal adhesions involving calcified intestinal loops.
Which one of the following is the MOST appropriate next step in management of this patient?

options.A: Initiate broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.B: Repeat ascites study
options.C: Perform a diagnostic laparoscope exploration
options.D: Treat with prednisolone and tamoxifen
